ideas.title: Zap a friend: static you carry
ideas.goal: The player rubs Lumi's feathers on the sheep's wool and carries the charge: the sheep's fluff rises into a halo as Lumi creeps up, seeds and paper scraps leap to the beak, and touching Pinchy's nose throws a real spark. More rubbing, a longer spark. On a rainy day the charge leaks away before you get there, so you learn when and how to sneak up. A prank you replay, and the friends are on the receiving end for once.
ideas.toward: The island's first electric field and first spark. The same solver later gives capacitor voltages (a Leyden jar of brine in a bottle is the next step) and the circuits' potentials.
ideas.idea: No animation is triggered by a charge level. Charge moves by contact and rubbing work, according to the materials' places in the triboelectric series (a column in the materials table). Conductors are equipotentials solved by the em.jl boundary-element solver (the one that already does magnets' surface charges), so every body's potential and the field everywhere come from where the bodies are. Wool and crest strands are simulated fibre chains (bending stiffness, weight), each segment carrying its share of charge, so the field pushes them apart into the halo by Coulomb's law. Seeds and paper scraps are rigid bodies feeling the same field. A spark happens where the solved gap field passes Paschen's breakdown for that gap, and it carries the stored energy (1/2 C V^2) away as a blue streak and a sound. Humidity from the weather sets the surface leakage.
ideas.form: a sneak-up interaction in the human's game; a traced close film at dusk, Lumi's head and the sheep in frame: the halo rising as Lumi approaches, then the spark lighting both faces

ideas.title: Copper from green water, on anything iron
ideas.goal: The player crushes green rock, soaks it in sour fruit water until the water turns blue-green, then dips anything iron into it: a spike, the crab's hat buckle, the crane's hook. It comes out copper-coated, and the longer it stays in, the thicker the coat, passing through rainbow tints first. Copper without a kiln. Friends bring their iron things to be plated.
ideas.toward: Copper from green rock by a second, chemical road (the road step), and the first cell: iron and copper in an electrolyte is a battery, so the same bath later gives current through a wire.
ideas.idea: Malachite dissolves in acid at a rate set by the crushed surface and the acid's strength, giving a copper ion concentration that sets the water's colour (absorption of Cu2+, a real Hikari medium). An iron object in it displaces copper (Fe + Cu2+ -> Fe2+ + Cu) at a rate set by its wetted area and the concentration, and the deposited thickness follows by Faraday's law. The surface renders as a thin copper film over iron: Hikari's thin-film interference gives the real rainbow tints at tens of nanometres before it turns solid copper. The bath depletes, so big jobs need fresh green water.
ideas.form: a workbench process the player does step by step in the human's game; a traced macro film of a spike in the blue-green bath with Lumi's beak holding it, colour creeping up the iron

ideas.title: Lightning makes a lodestone
ideas.goal: When the storm rolls in, the player races to plant copper rods and iron spikes on the hill before it arrives. The strike picks its own path through what stands there: a good rod takes it safely into the ground, a lone iron spike comes out a magnet, and you dig glass roots out of the sand where it went in. You make magnet stones by catching lightning.
ideas.toward: Where magnet stones come from (real lodestones are magnetised by lightning), conductors against insulators, and the big shared moment of the road.
ideas.idea: Step by step, the downward leader moves where the electrostatic field is strongest. That field is the same em.jl solve as the static one, with the cloud's charge layer above and the conductors the player placed, so a rod raises the field at its tip. It attaches when the gap to a conductor's tip is within the striking distance for that peak current (r = 10 I^0.65, the standard's own law). The return stroke follows a real current waveform (the IEC 62305 10/350 microsecond pulse). Its Biot-Savart field magnetises the iron it passes through softiron.jl's hysteresis. Its Joule heat in the sand, from the current density, melts a glass root wherever the energy passes sand's melting point. Wood in the path chars in the fire model.
ideas.form: a storm event the player plays in the human's game; a traced film at night lit only by the strike, then Lumi's beak holding the spike over pins that leap to it

ideas.title: Treasure hunting with a needle
ideas.goal: The player walks the island with a magnetised needle hanging from Lumi's beak. Over buried iron ore it dips and swings, so you map the island by walking and dig where it pulls hardest, finding ore lumps, an old anchor or a lost spike. Every island seed hides its ore differently, and better needles (longer, stronger magnetised) find deeper ore.
ideas.toward: Gathering the iron the builds need, by the real field, and a reason to make better magnets: the field solver answers the player's question 'where is the iron?'.
ideas.idea: Ore bodies are magnetised volumes under the ground, and their anomaly field at the surface comes from em.jl (dipole sums or surface charges), on top of the island's background field. The needle is a rigid body on a cord: its weight, its moment and the cord's swing give the dip and the jitter, and Lumi's walking motion shakes it, so you learn to stand still. Digging is the existing ground editing.
ideas.form: an exploration play in the human's game, walking Lumi; a traced film following Lumi across the meadow, the needle in the beak swinging, then the spade finding the lump
